text:
julia: heads up — canary for v2.5.1 showing a p95 latency drift at ~30% traffic :thinking_face:
deploy-bot: rollout: v2.5.1 -> 30% traffic in us-west2. metrics: p95=820ms (baseline 420ms), errors 0.5% 
 mike: saw that in the dashboard. is this steady or a spike?
 julia: it’s been climbing for last 8 minutes, trending up across multiple pods.
 ashley: any correlation with batch size or recent kernel flags? I don’t see config changes in the diff.
 deploy-bot: note: automatic rollback window active. autorevert threshold: p95>750ms sustained 5m. current state: threshold breached 3m ago.
 pm-ron: if deploy-bot would auto-revert we need a customer note queued. are we okay with autopilot for this one?
 ops-jen: suggest manual hold — traffic still healthy and no user errors. we can pin the traffic and run a quick health probe on kv-cache.
 mike: +1 to hold. we should run a targeted canary flush on two pods, try a restart, and check kernel flag toggles.
 julia: i'll pin rollout at 30% and add a manual hold tag. can someone grab the runbook?
 ashley: grabbing runbook now: /runbooks/rollback-checklist. steps: 1) pin rollout 2) collect p95 by pod 3) restart pod pair 4) if persists, rollback to v2.5.0
 deploy-bot: action: traffic pinned at 30% by julia. autopilot rollback suppressed by manual hold.
 mike: logs from pod-07 show increased attention latency around token 512 boundary. might be a model kernel regression.
 julia: good catch. if it's kernel-related we should rollback rather than hotfix. rollback will restore quantization kernel v1.3 behavior.
 pm-ron: customer comms draft: "We paused the canary for v2.5.1 due to increased latency in a subset of requests. We're investigating and will either resume or roll back. No customer-facing errors observed." ok to send after ops-jen thumbs up? :email:
 ops-jen: OK to send, please tag support for watch.
 deploy-bot: suggested rollback target: v2.5.0 (pinned build 20260321.2). estimated time to rollback: ~4m, can cause short rolling restarts.
 julia: do we want to do immediate rollback or attempt quick pod restarts first?
 mike: try two node restarts first — low impact. if p95 doesn't drop below 550ms in 6m, rollback.
 ashley: started restarts on pod-06 and pod-07 now. will report metrics in 2m.
 sre-bot: alert: p95 reduced to 510ms on pod-07 after restart. cluster p95 now 560ms.
 julia: nice, looks promising. keep pinned and monitor for 10m. if it re-escalates we execute rollback.
 pm-ron: leaving customer note as "paused" for now. will update if we roll back.
 mike: logging this decision: reason=canary-p95-drift, action=manual-hold+pod-restart, rollback-if=6m sustained >650ms, rollback-target=v2.5.0
 ashley: adding release notes change: rollforward blocked until postmortem.
 julia: thanks everyone. will unpin and roll back only if threshold triggers. I'll update thread in 10m. :hourglass:
